out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. Please have the employee health document signed by all the food employees by the follow up date.

out_items.name: Proper cooling time and temperature

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. Observed cooked chicken (45-48 F) not properly cooled in the walk in cooler. The chicken was left in the unit for two days. The chicken was tightly packed in a plastic container covered with a lid.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. CDI: The chicken was discarded. EHS discussed proper cooling methods.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: container of heavy cream (48 F) on a container lid in the prep unit on the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: PIC used heavy cream in cooking.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): biryani, masala sauce, yogurt, sauce, and tomato sauce.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. CDI: EHS provided the document. Document was filled out during the inspection.

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: biryani, masala sauce, yogurt sauce, and tomato sauce.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CDI: PIC time stamped all the foods with start and end times.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cooked chicken (45-48 F) in the walk in cooler. The chicken was date marked 9/9 and was not taken out of the unit since then. The chicken was tightly packed in a plastic container covered with a lid. The temperature of the unit read 37 F.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: The chicken was discarded. EHS discussed proper cooling methods.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: container of cooked onion sauce placed on a dry storage shelf at 29 F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. CDI: The food was relocated to the walk in cooler.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Rear door, the kitchen is being propped open for ventilation without an effective means or barriers for preventing pest entry.
violations.corrective_action: Provide screens (16 mesh to 1 inch), air curtains, or other effective means to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. PIC closed rear door in the kitchen. Agreed to install a screen door if they wish to keep it open for ventilation.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Ice As Coolant Not Used as Food
violations.observation: I’m served in the bar ice machine that ice being used for food was also being used as a coolant, medium for bottled beer and bottled tonics and seltzer water.
violations.corrective_action: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food, packaged foods, beverages, or cooling coils/tubes, the ice may not be used as food. PIC remove the bottle from the beverage ice. EHS spoke to PIC about separation of ice being used as a coolant, medium versus ice being used as beverage.

violations.title: Unpackaged Food Preparation, No Contamination
violations.observation: Observed unpackaged spices on a spice rack, being left, uncovered, and being exposed to potential contamination next to the cook line.
violations.corrective_action: During preparation, unpackaged food, shall be protected from environmental contamination. PIC established lids for uncovered spices.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed in the kitchen area root ginger, whole potatoes, premade sauces, stored on the floor
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS asked the PIC move the ginger potato and premade sauces onto shelving that is at least 6 inches off the floor Nawabi Hyderabad House Indian Restaurant. (Inspection Date: 08/06/2025) Page 3 of 5

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: Observed wiping rags being used to cover RTE foods.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. EHS formed PIC that only approved food contact services are permitted to be used to cover ready to eat foods PIC removed rags and covered foods within an approved food contact surface.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: EHS observed throughout the kitchen, wet, wiping rags are being stored on counters and on food prep surfaces, not in sanitizer solution buckets.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. PIC moved wet wiping rags to sanitizer solution buckets.

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Laundered
violations.observation: Wiping cloths improperly stored between use, not in chemical sanitizing solution, in the following locations: observed soiled, wiping s not being laundered on a daily basis
violations.corrective_action: Cloths in use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be laundered daily. PIC removed soiled, wiping class to be laundered. Replaced with clean wiping cloth. Nawabi Hyderabad House Indian Restaurant. (Inspection Date: 08/06/2025) Page 4 of 5

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: observed a plastic bowl to go, contain her being used as a dispensing utensil for chicken in the three door prep top across from the line
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC removed the to go container bowl reviewed proper handle requirements of in use utensils

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not designed or constructed to be easily cleanable: observed a one by six plank of wood being suspended over the center island of the kitchen and being utilized as a mounting point for electrical outlets.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. EHS informed PIC that untreated lumber is not permitted within kitchens. PIC agreed to replace one by six plank of wood by next inspection.

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: two door under counter fridge across from the oven was observed at 69F internal.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. PIC called repair company to correct two door under counter fridge to ensure it holds below 41F internal.

out_items.name: Warewashing facilities installed, maintained and used; test strips

violations.title: Test Kit/Device for Chemical Sanitizer
violations.observation: Observe no test kit in the facility available quaternary ammonia dispenser at the three compartment sink
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a @BLEACH, QUATERNARY AMMONIA, IODINE@ test kit. PIC ordered new test kit for quaternary ammonia. Nawabi Hyderabad House Indian Restaurant. (Inspection Date: 08/06/2025) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Equipment Clean to Sight and Touch
violations.observation: Observed the six Burner Grill in need of cleaning, equipment was not clean to sight and touch
violations.corrective_action: The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. PIC agreed to clean grill by next inspection.

violations.title: Equipment Clean to Sight and Touch
violations.observation: Observed on prep tables throughout the kitchen area, leftover rice and food from the previous day. Equipment was not clean to site and touch.
violations.corrective_action: The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. PIC had employees, clean prep tables and other equipment so it was clean to sight and touch.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.observation: Observed five ceiling tiles missing throughout the kitchen area
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. EHS informed PIC that facility was to be maintained in good repair, PiC agreed to replace ceiling tiles.
